name: python_exec
description: Run SANDBOXED Python (numpy/Pillow/pandas, WASM) for array/pixel/spatial/table work better done in Python than JS — pixel-mask & centroid a target, count regions, BFS a maze, or SUM/AVG/GROUP a table. Your inputs are ALREADY loaded as variables — `image`→`img`/`img_np` (PIL + H×W×3 uint8), `tables`→DataFrame(s) — so reference them directly, never re-open/parse/read_csv them. `return` a value → comes back as TEXT (or set `cast` to mint a clickable @pt/@box). RETURN TYPE auto-renders: a sympy expression → typeset LaTeX, a PIL Image (or to_base64()) or a matplotlib figure (returned, or just left open) → an image, a DataFrame → a table — so just `return sympy.diff(...)` / `return img` and cite `![…](@tool:…:out)` (no cast; add `| raw` to force the literal text). Each call is STATELESS — a fresh namespace, nothing persists. In scope: numpy (np), PIL (Image), pandas (pd), scipy (import scipy), sympy (symbolic math; `import sympy; sympy.latex(expr)` → a `| latex` string), pyarrow (pd.read_parquet / to_parquet / read_feather; Arrow IPC via pyarrow.ipc), matplotlib (`import matplotlib.pyplot as plt`) + stdlib (io, math, collections, itertools…). A cell the read-only dialect covers runs without asking; any other asks the user first. No network or filesystem here: use fetch_url for that. Details: `agent_api_docs({ tool: "python_exec" })`.

code.description: Python. Reference img/img_np/your DataFrame(s); end with a `return` OR a bare trailing expression (Jupyter-style: a last line `df` is the result). print() is captured as stdout.

image.description: Optional CSS selector or @pt:/@box: token to load as img/img_np. An @box loads the exact container content; an @pt loads a square neighbourhood around the point.

cast.description: 'pt' or 'box': the return is a clickable point ([x,y]) or box ([x1,y1,x2,y2]) in the input image's pixels, placed on the page for you.

verify.description: Look at an image result (a chart) before citing it. Default false.

margin.description: For an @pt image only: the crop RADIUS in px around the point (a bigger margin = more context). Omit for the default. Ignored for @box / CSS selectors.

tables.description: Spreadsheet/table data → pandas DataFrame(s). Table(s) to load, ALREADY parsed (never re-read them): one source → `df`, or { name: source } → each under its name, a Python variable name (e.g. { sales: … }). A source: a page <table> selector, a Google Sheets URL, a URL fetch_url read, or an `@tool:` pointer to a table.

tableRaw.description: Load table cells as raw STRINGS (skip the default numeric/currency auto-cast). Use only for ZIP/SKU/leading-zero IDs that casting would corrupt.

maxChars.description: Raise the per-slot output truncation for THIS call (default 2000, max 20000). A raise needs human approval + `maxCharsReason`. Prefer returning a compact result.

maxCharsReason.description: Why this call needs more than the default 2000 chars — required when `maxChars` exceeds it; shown to the human on the approval card.

revises.description: If this is a RETRY of an earlier call, its pointer (`@tool:abc1234`, `@tool:python_exec`, or `@tool:"a label"`). The panel then shows the human a diff of what changed. Changes nothing about how this runs.

changed.description: One line on what you changed, shown beside that diff. Only with `revises`.

token.description: `true`, or a short label ("the pricing table"): keep a handle to this output.

title.description: What this call is for, in a few words.
